what: agent-connect-plan.md step 7.1 item 0.3, the notification checks, recorded on 2026-11-26

control: the server's notification resolved with no error and nothing reached the session
a server given with --mcp-config is not found by server:<name> ('no MCP server configured with that name'); it must be in the project's .mcp.json

runs.note: crashed before init: the flag is variadic and took the prompt as an entry ('entries must be tagged')
no development-channel warning was shown and no 'Channels (experimental)' notice; the job's respawn flags do not carry the channel flag

runs.start: interactive with the flag, warning accepted, one turn, then /background

c.result: recorded from the changelog and documentation; one configuration measured
c.minimumVersion: 2.1.80 (channels added); 2.1.81 permission relay; 2.1.128 a Console API key; 2.1.234 permission requests only to servers registered as channels
c.authentication: Anthropic authentication: a claude.ai login or a Console API key; not on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry. Pro, Max and Ultra users without an organisation skip the organisation checks. claude.ai Team and Enterprise: blocked until an Owner sets channelsEnabled. Console with managed settings: blocked until channelsEnabled is set.
c.measured: 2.1.332 with a claude.ai individual login: the development channel registers and delivers (item a)
c.alsoFound: On the v2 MCP client a channel server that negotiates MCP revision 2026-07-28 is not registered as a channel (docs, mcp.md 'Push messages with channels'); MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy keeps stdio servers on the earlier handshake.

d.summary: A SessionStart hook with asyncRewake that exits 2 wakes an idle session.

runs.note: delivered as a task-notification headed 'Stop hook feedback', its text labelled 'Stop hook blocking error from command "SessionStart:startup"'; one wake per hook run

e.summary: A skill arms Monitor on inbox.sh --follow; lines reach an idle session, the watch expires, the session re-arms it on the expiry notice, and lines after the re-arm arrive. The same in a claude --bg session.
e.framing: each line arrives as <task-notification><summary>Monitor event: "<description>"</summary><event>LINE</event></task-notification>; the expiry as '[Monitor expired after 1m with 1 event delivered. Re-arm it if you still need the watch.]'
e.limits: timeout_ms defaults to 300000 and is capped at 1800000; a line written between the expiry and the re-arm is not seen by a tail that starts at the end (tail -n 0)
